compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The mcp blue-green deploy block documents itself as INDEPENDENT of the review-bot block above
it, but it sits AFTER that block's `exit 0`. When the review-bot is busy, the deferral path
terminates the whole script, so the mcp deploy never runs. The documented independence is false
in the only case where it matters — a shared `src/rebar` change, which triggers BOTH triggers.

## The coupling, in the code

The mcp blue-green block documents itself as "INDEPENDENT of the review-bot block above", but
it sits AFTER that block's `exit 0`. When a review is in flight the drain gate defers and exits
the whole PROCESS, so the mcp block is never reached. Both trigger lists start with `src/rebar`,
so any library change matches BOTH — and the bot drains with a single worker, making
`in_flight > 0` its normal state.

## Observed impact (2026-08-26)

The bot drains with a single worker, so `in_flight > 0` is its normal state and ~every tick
deferred. Two commits merged at 06:47Z were still not running forty minutes later, with
`deploy_deferrals` at 2-3 per five-minute bucket. One was the mcp secrets-refresh fix, so the
deploy path could not repair itself.

## Why the alarm did not catch it

`deploy_deferrals` counts deferrals, and deferring is CORRECT for the bot — nothing failed.

## Proposed fix

Scope the deferral to the bot block instead of terminating the script. `autodeploy.sh` is a
linear oneshot with no enclosing loop, so `continue` is not available: HOIST the bot block into
a new function `deploy_review_bot`, and have the deferral set `bot_deferred=1` and `return 0`
from it. Control then reaches the mcp block. The mcp path is a pointer-swap that never kills an
in-flight op, so it has no reason to wait on the bot's drain. The function wrapper also keeps
indentation unchanged, so the diff stays a few hunks instead of re-indenting fifty lines.

**The tick still stops before the footer.** Letting control past the old `exit 0` must not turn
a deferred tick into a completed one, so a guard placed AFTER the mcp block and BEFORE the
host-observability re-materialization, the certbot re-materialization, and the footer exits
when the bot deferred (or when either component was skipped with a delta still pending). Those
two intervening blocks are therefore skipped on a deferred tick exactly as the old `exit 0`
skipped them — no re-materialization runs that did not run before. Everything the footer does is therefore skipped exactly as the `exit 0` skipped it:
`deployed-sha` and both component markers stay unadvanced, and `rm -f "$DEFER_FILE"` does not
run — the deferral EPISODE carries forward, which is what keeps `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` reachable.
Clearing it on a deferred tick would reset the bound every tick and the gate would defer
forever instead of eventually recreating the container. The ONLY behavioural difference from
the pre-fix path is that the mcp block above already ran.

Take care that the deferral episode bookkeeping (`DEFER_FILE`, `:538`) and the
`record_backoff_failure` semantics stay unchanged for the bot path, and that a bot deferral
still results in the same exit status the timer expects when the mcp block also does nothing.

## Test gap that let this through

`test_shared_src_change_triggers_both_targets` drives a shared change but with the bot IDLE, so
it never reaches the deferral path. The uncovered case is a shared change while the bot is BUSY.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A tick where the review-bot block DEFERS still reaches the mcp blue-green block, so a
      shared `src/rebar` change deploys the mcp service without waiting on the bot's drain.
      Proof: `test_bot_deferral_still_reaches_the_mcp_blue_green_deploy` — restoring the
      `exit 0` turns it RED.
- [x] The bot path's deferral bookkeeping is preserved: it still defers while a review is in
      flight, the episode file and `DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX` bound carry forward, and a deferred tick
      still records nothing as complete.
      Proof: same test — it asserts deployed-sha unadvanced and the defer file preserved;
      clearing the defer file above the guard turns it RED on that assertion specifically.
- [x] Regression coverage drives a tick with BOTH triggers matching and the bot busy, asserting
      the mcp container is still deployed.
      Proof: `test_bot_deferral_still_reaches_the_mcp_blue_green_deploy`
- [x] The stub reports a shared `src/rebar` change rather than forcing the bot block false.
      Proof: `_GIT_STUB_SHARED_SRC` answers the path list it is asked about.
- [x] mcp does not re-deploy on every tick of a deferral episode. Added after review: without
      it the fix trades "mcp never deploys" for "mcp redeploys every two minutes".
      Proof: `test_repeated_deferred_ticks_do_not_redeploy_mcp_every_time`, and
      `test_a_complete_tick_advances_the_mcp_marker_even_when_mcp_was_a_no_op` for the
      footer's lockstep write. Both mutation-checked.


## Verification

    .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_review_drain.py -q -p no:randomly
    bash -n infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh && shellcheck -S error infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh

The new coverage has teeth when: with the `exit 0` restored in the deferral path, the new
both-triggers test FAILS (no mcp deploy), and with the scoped `return` fix it PASSES.

## Scope note

The per-component work that grew out of code review — `mcp-deployed-sha` / `bot-deployed-sha`
markers, the mcp-scoped backoff, and the `bot_incomplete` / `mcp_incomplete` flags — has been
SPLIT OUT to `symbiotic-cold-flee`, with the operator's approval. This ticket is now
exactly what it was filed as: scoping the review-bot deferral so control reaches the mcp block.
Keeping them together made one plan describe two changes, which is how the plan and the
implementation drifted apart across nine review rounds.

file_impact.reason: Scope the review-bot deferral to that block (flag + skip the rest of the bot block) instead of exit 0, so control reaches the mcp blue-green block which is documented as independent and never waits on an in-flight review

Drive a tick with BOTH triggers matching and the bot busy: the mcp deploy must still happen. The current git stub reports only Dockerfile.mcp so the bot block is never entered, which is why this regressed unnoticed
